chat.author: Mark Atwood
chat.text: Client attestation should stay optional. An AS that requires it shuts out open-source and self-built clients, which have no one to attest them. Use it to raise limits, not as a gate. As a co-author of OAuth 1.0a: we wrote in §11.7 that a freely available client's secret can be extracted, so a server shouldn't rely on it alone to identify the client. Attestation doesn't change that; it just limits OAuth to clients a platform vendor will vouch for.

Karl, Thanks for including Actor Chain in the related work.
Our February/March SPICE drafts documented actor-signed history, selective disclosure and AS commitments; we presented at IETF 125. Current Actor Chain supports original proofs/AS acceptances for selected actors while omitting intermediary records; membership/order remain AS-attested.
